title: The impact of vehicle miles traveled and urban form on air pollution
abstract: • Urban form can affect the relationship between VMT and air quality. • Few studies have examined this relationship due to data constraints. • In urban counties, we find positive correlations between VMT and air pollution. • In rural counties, VMT had statistically insignificant impacts on air pollution. • This implies reducing VMT in urban areas could have a larger air pollution effect. In the past century, there have been major shifts in the built and natural environment across the U.S. as urban areas grow to accommodate larger urban populations. Yet, there is little research on how these changes in urban form could affect an important relationship in transportation and health: vehicle miles traveled (VMT) and air pollution. For example, studies show urban areas typically have a higher building density, which can trap in more air pollution relative to rural or open spaces where pollution can disperse more widely. A lack of detailed data on VMT, as well as methodological challenges have made assessing this relationship difficult. To address this, we use a quasi-experimental framework and a unique dataset to examine how a dramatic change in vehicle miles traveled (VMT) during the COVID-19 pandemic affected air pollution and if or how urban form moderated this relationship. We use detailed county-level daily VMT and air quality data in the contiguous U.S. between January and August 2020. Our results show statistically significant positive correlations between VMT and air pollution in urban counties, but in rural counties the marginal effect of VMT on air pollution was either statistically insignificant or very small. Results from this study suggest that efforts to reduce the marginal impact of VMT or vehicle emissions in urban areas could lead to a greater improvement in air quality when compared to more rural counties due to the built environment.
abstract_zh: • 城市形态会影响车辆行驶里程（VMT）与空气质量之间的关系。• 由于数据限制，很少有研究考察这一关系。• 在城市县，我们发现车辆行驶里程与空气污染之间存在正相关。• 在农村县，车辆行驶里程对空气污染的影响在统计上不显著。• 这意味着，减少城市地区的车辆行驶里程可能会产生更大的空气污染减排效果。在过去一个世纪里，随着城市地区扩张以容纳更多的城市人口，美国的建成环境和自然环境发生了重大变化。然而，关于这些城市形态变化如何影响交通与健康中的一个重要关系——车辆行驶里程（VMT）与空气污染之间的关系——的研究却很少。例如，研究表明，城市地区的建筑密度通常较高，相较于农村或开阔空间，这更容易使空气污染滞留，后者的污染物则能更广泛地扩散。车辆行驶里程的详细数据匮乏，以及方法上的挑战，使得评估这一关系十分困难。为此，我们采用准实验框架和一个独特的数据集，考察了COVID-19大流行期间车辆行驶里程的剧烈变化如何影响空气污染，以及城市形态是否以及如何调节这一关系。我们使用了2020年1月至8月美国本土各县每日车辆行驶里程和空气质量的详细数据。结果表明，在城市县，车辆行驶里程与空气污染之间存在统计上显著的正相关，而在农村县，车辆行驶里程对空气污染的边际影响在统计上不显著或非常小。本研究结果表明，与农村县相比，由于建成环境的原因，减少城市地区车辆行驶里程的边际影响，或减少车辆排放的努力，可能会带来更大的空气质量改善。

Emission standards, public transit, and infant health
venue: Journal of Policy Analysis and Management
abstract: Transit buses are an integral part of urban life. They reduce externalities generated from private vehicles and increase geographic mobility. However, unlike most private vehicles in the United States, they use diesel fuel and emit higher amounts of toxic pollutants. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency set emission standards for transit buses starting in 1988 that have been continually updated, but their public health and economic impacts are unclear due to scarce emissions data. I construct a novel panel dataset for the New York City (NYC) Transit bus fleet between 1990 and 2009 and examine the impact of bus pollution on infant health by using bus vintage as a proxy for emissions. I exploit the variation in vintage as older buses are retired and replaced with newer, lower‐emitting buses forced to adhere to stricter emission standards. I then assign maternal exposure to bus vintage at the census block level. Findings suggest that maternal exposure to the oldest, unregulated buses is associated with modest reductions in birth weight and gestational age relative to newer buses that abide by emissions policies. I then conduct a back‐of‐the‐envelope cost‐benefit calculation and find net economic benefits of $53.3 million resulting from improved emission standards for the 2009 birth cohort in NYC. Since the treatment in this study clearly maps to federal emissions policies, these results are the first to provide credible evidence that transit bus emission standards had a positive effect on infant health.
abstract_zh: 公交巴士是城市生活不可或缺的一部分。它们减少了私家车产生的外部性，并提高了地理上的流动性。然而，与美国大多数私家车不同，公交巴士使用柴油，并排放更多有毒污染物。美国环境保护署自1988年起为公交巴士设定了排放标准，并不断更新，但由于排放数据稀缺，其对公共健康和经济的影响尚不明确。我构建了一个新颖的面板数据集，涵盖1990年至2009年纽约市（NYC）公交车队，并通过使用车辆车龄作为排放的代理变量，考察了公交车污染对婴儿健康的影响。我利用了车龄的变化：随着旧车退役，并被必须遵守更严格排放标准的新型低排放车辆所取代。随后，我在人口普查街区层面为母亲分配了所接触的公交车车龄。研究结果表明，与遵守排放政策的新型公交车相比，母亲暴露于最老旧、未受监管的公交车，与出生体重和孕周的适度降低相关。随后，我进行了粗略的成本效益计算，发现纽约市2009年出生队列因排放标准改善而获得的净经济效益为5330万美元。由于本研究的处理明确对应于联邦排放政策，这些结果首次提供了可信的证据，表明公交巴士排放标准对婴儿健康产生了积极影响。

Analyzing the relationship between bus pollution policies and morbidity using a quasi-experiment
abstract: Transit buses are used by millions of commuters every day, but they emit toxic diesel fumes. In 1988, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency implemented emission standards for transit buses, which have been continually updated. Yet there is no quantitative evidence of the health benefits from these bus pollution policies due to data constraints and confounding variables. In this study, a quasi-experiment is used to exploit the geographic and temporal variation in emission standards by using bus vintage as a proxy for bus emissions. This is accomplished using a unique, rich panel data set, which includes daily information on bus vintage and route for the New York City Transit bus fleet between 2006 and 2009. This information is merged with daily data on emergency department (ED) visits for respiratory illnesses, which include patients' residences at the census block level and exact admission date. Economic benefits resulting from these bus pollution policies are then estimated. Results show that stricter transit bus emission standards by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency for particulate matter are associated with reduced ED visits for respiratory diseases for patients living within a few hundred feet of a bus route. These findings demonstrate that bus pollution policies have made critical improvements to public health.
abstract_zh: 数百万通勤者每天都乘坐公交巴士，但它们会排放有毒的柴油废气。1988年，美国环境保护署对公交巴士实施了排放标准，并不断更新。然而，由于数据限制和混杂变量的存在，目前尚无关于这些巴士污染政策健康效益的定量证据。在本研究中，我们采用准实验方法，利用车辆车龄作为巴士排放的代理变量，挖掘排放标准在地理和时间上的差异。这一研究依托于一个独特而丰富的面板数据集，该数据集包含2006年至2009年纽约市公交车队的每日车龄和线路信息。该信息与呼吸系统疾病的每日急诊就诊数据相匹配，后者包括患者在人口普查街区层面的居住地和确切入院日期。随后，我们估算了这些巴士污染政策产生的经济效益。结果表明，美国环境保护署针对颗粒物实施的更严格的公交巴士排放标准，与居住在公交线路几百英尺范围内的患者呼吸系统疾病急诊就诊次数的减少相关。这些发现表明，巴士污染政策对公共健康作出了关键性改善。
